simple.meaning: זְמָן (zᵉmân) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an appointed occasion.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Nehemiah, Esther, Ecclesiastes, beginning at Nehemiah 2:6. Its contexts include family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זְמָן (H2165).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: זְמָן (zᵉmân) / H2165 is traced through Nehemiah 2:6, Esther 9:27, Esther 9:31, Ecclesiastes 3:1 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The king said to me (the queen was also sitting by him), “How long will your journey be? When will you return?”

timeline.evidenceText: The king said to me (the queen was also sitting by him), “How long will your journey be? When will you return?”

the Jews established and imposed on themselves, and on their descendants, and on all those who joined themselves to them, so that it should not fail that they would keep these two days according to what was written, and according to its appointed time, every year;

to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants, in the matter of the fastings and their cry.
For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:

definitions.full: H2165. zeman זְמָ֑ן noun masculine (late) appointed time, time (Arabic , Ethiopic Biblical Aramaic, זְמַן ᵑ7 , but Syriac , Mandean זיבנא , Samaritan , Palmyrene זבנא , compare Reckend ZMG 1888, 394 **Mandean זנאן , see Nö M 152 ; on Old Persian origin see Biblical Aramaic) — singular זְמָ֑ן Neh 2:6 ; Eccl 3:1 ; suffix וְכִזְמַנָּ֑ם Est 9:27 , בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶם 9:31 , (on Dagh. compare Ges § 20 . 2, c).
